name: Parker
summary: Flies through the Sun's outer atmosphere, closer than any spacecraft before it.
milestones: Dec 2024 — record pass 6.1 million km above the surface, at 192 km/s
2026 — still diving through the corona every 88 days

name: Solar Orbiter
summary: Images the Sun from close range while tilting its orbit to look down on the poles.
milestones: Mar 2025 — first views of the Sun's poles from outside the plane of the planets
Dec 2026 — a Venus flyby raises the orbit's tilt to 24°

name: BepiColombo
summary: Two orbiters — Europe's MPO and Japan's Mio — to map Mercury and its magnetic field.
milestones: 2018–2025 — nine planetary flybys (Earth, Venus twice, Mercury six times)
21 Nov 2026 — captured into Mercury orbit, only the second mission ever to get there
Dec 2026 — the two orbiters separate
Apr 2027 — science phase begins

name: DAVINCI
summary: Drops a probe through Venus's atmosphere, sampling its gases all the way down to the surface.
milestones: 2021 — selected in the Discovery programme
2026 — reported as a cancellation target in the 2027 budget request; the Senate bill funds it

name: VERITAS
summary: Maps Venus by radar to find out whether its volcanoes and tectonics are still active.
milestones: 2021 — selected in the Discovery programme
2026 — reported as a cancellation target in the 2027 budget request; the Senate bill funds it

name: EnVision
summary: Europe's Venus orbiter: interior, surface and atmosphere studied together, with a NASA-built radar.
milestones: 2033 — arrival, then aerobraking down to the science orbit

name: Chang'e 6
summary: Brought back the first samples from the far side of the Moon — 1.9 kg of them.
milestones: Jun 2024 — lands in Apollo crater, inside the South Pole–Aitken basin
25 Jun 2024 — the capsule lands in Inner Mongolia

name: Artemis II
summary: Four astronauts flew around the Moon and back — the first crew beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
milestones: 1 Apr 2026 — launch on the Space Launch System
6 Apr 2026 — passes Apollo 13's distance record
11 Apr 2026 — the capsule Integrity splashes down in the Pacific

name: Artemis III
summary: A crewed flight in Earth orbit to rehearse docking with the commercial lunar landers — not a landing.

name: Chang'e 7
summary: Hunts for water ice at the south pole, with a hopping probe built to jump into permanently shadowed craters.
milestones: Aug 2026 — on the pad at Wenchang when bad weather postponed the launch; now expected in 2027

name: Artemis IV
summary: Planned as the first crewed Moon landing since Apollo 17.

name: Curiosity
summary: Has been climbing Mount Sharp since 2012, reading its layers for the story of Mars's water.

name: Perseverance
summary: Drills and caches rock cores in an ancient river delta — the samples a return mission would fetch.
milestones: Feb 2021 — lands in Jezero with the Ingenuity helicopter
2026 — the 2027 budget request would trim its funding

name: ESCAPADE
summary: Two small orbiters to measure how the solar wind strips away Mars's atmosphere.
milestones: Nov 2025 — launched
Nov 2026 — swings past Earth to set course for Mars
2027 — arrival

name: MMX
agency: JAXA, with NASA, ESA, CNES, DLR
summary: Will land on Mars's moon Phobos, collect about 10 g of it and bring the sample home in 2031.
milestones: 20 Oct 2026 — launched on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima
2027 — arrives in Mars orbit
2029 — the Franco-German rover Idefix lands on Phobos
2031 — sample returns to Earth

name: Rosalind Franklin
summary: Europe's rover, with a 2-metre drill to look for traces of life below the radiation-scoured surface.
budgetNote: Figures are NASA's contribution to the ESA mission.

name: Tianwen-3
summary: China's Mars sample return, aiming to have samples on Earth around 2031.

name: SR-1 / SkyFall
summary: A fission-powered ion-drive spacecraft carrying three Ingenuity-class helicopters to scout Mars from the air.
milestones: Mar 2026 — announced, reusing hardware built for the lunar Gateway
About a year after launch — arrives and releases the helicopters
budgetNote: The Senate figure is the Mars Future Missions line, which includes SkyFall.

name: Mars Sample Return
summary: Would bring Perseverance's cached samples to Earth — the top priority of the last planetary decadal survey.
milestones: Jan 2026 — the 2026 budget ends support for the programme in its existing form
Nov 2026 — the Senate's 2027 bill would revive it inside the Moon-to-Mars programme
budgetNote: The Senate bill moves it to the Moon-to-Mars programme as a demonstration for human missions.

name: Dawn
summary: The first spacecraft to orbit two worlds beyond Earth, and the first to reach a dwarf planet.
milestones: 2011–2012 — orbits Vesta
Mar 2015 — enters orbit at Ceres
Nov 2018 — runs out of fuel; it still circles Ceres

name: OSIRIS-APEX
summary: Delivered samples of asteroid Bennu in 2023 and is now chasing Apophis, to arrive just after its 2029 Earth flyby.
milestones: Oct 2020 — grabs a sample of Bennu
Sep 2023 — the sample capsule lands in Utah
13 Apr 2029 — Apophis passes inside geostationary orbit; the rendezvous follows

name: Lucy
summary: Tours the Trojan asteroids that share Jupiter's orbit — leftovers from the building of the giant planets.
milestones: 2023, 2025 — rehearsal flybys of Dinkinesh and Donaldjohanson
2027–2028 — four Trojans in the leading swarm, starting with Eurybates
2033 — the Patroclus–Menoetius pair in the trailing swarm

name: Psyche
summary: Heading for a metal-rich asteroid that may be the exposed core of a planet that never finished forming.
milestones: 15 May 2026 — gravity assist 4,500 km above Mars

name: Hera
summary: Europe's planetary-defence mission: surveys the asteroid moon that NASA's DART knocked off course in 2022.
milestones: Mar 2025 — Mars flyby
Nov 2026 — arrives at the Didymos pair, a month ahead of the original plan
At least six months of close-up study follow

name: Tianwen-2
summary: Samples a small asteroid that shadows Earth around the Sun, then flies on to a comet in the asteroid belt.
milestones: 7 Jun 2026 — enters orbit at Kamoʻoalewa
2027 — sample capsule due back at Earth
mid-2030s — reaches comet 311P/PANSTARRS

name: NEO Surveyor
summary: An infrared telescope built to find the hazardous asteroids that visible-light surveys miss.

name: Cassini–Huygens
summary: Thirteen years at Saturn: Enceladus's geysers, Titan's seas, and a final plunge into the planet.
milestones: Jan 2005 — the Huygens probe lands on Titan
Sep 2017 — Grand Finale

name: Juno
summary: Peers beneath Jupiter's clouds from a polar orbit; its extended mission added close passes of the moons.
milestones: Jul 2016 — enters orbit
2021–2024 — flybys of Ganymede, Europa and Io
2026 — close passes of the small inner moons Thebe and Adrastea

name: JUICE
summary: Europe's tour of Jupiter's icy moons, ending as the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than ours.
milestones: Aug 2024 — first lunar–Earth double flyby
Aug 2025 — Venus flyby
Jul 2031 — arrives at Jupiter
2034 — enters orbit around Ganymede

name: Europa Clipper
summary: Will skim past Europa about 50 times to learn whether the ocean under its ice could support life.
milestones: Mar 2025 — Mars gravity assist
3 Dec 2026 — Earth gravity assist
Apr 2030 — enters orbit around Jupiter

name: Dragonfly
summary: A car-sized octocopter that will hop between sites on Titan, sampling its organic chemistry.

name: Voyager 2
summary: Still the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune.
milestones: 1979–1989 — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus (1986) and Neptune (1989)
Nov 2018 — crosses into interstellar space
2035 — due to reach one light-day from Earth

name: Voyager 1
summary: The most distant human-made object: past Jupiter and Saturn, and in interstellar space since 2012.
milestones: 1979, 1980 — Jupiter and Saturn flybys
Aug 2012 — crosses into interstellar space
18 Nov 2026 — reaches one light-day from Earth, 25.9 billion km

name: New Horizons
summary: Showed us Pluto and the Kuiper belt object Arrokoth up close, and keeps sampling the outer heliosphere.
milestones: Jul 2015 — Pluto flyby
Jan 2019 — Arrokoth flyby

name: Uranus Orbiter
summary: The top new flagship of the 2023–2032 planetary decadal survey: the first orbiter at an ice giant.
budgetNote: The Senate bill directs NASA to start the project.

name: Hubble
summary: In orbit since 1990 and still NASA's workhorse in visible and ultraviolet light.

name: Chandra
summary: The sharpest X-ray eyes in orbit, watching black holes, supernova remnants and galaxy clusters.

name: JWST
summary: The 6.5-metre infrared flagship, reading the first galaxies and the air of exoplanets.

name: Roman
summary: Hubble-sharp images over a field 100 times wider, to map dark energy and take a census of cold exoplanets.
milestones: 30 Aug 2026 — launched on a Falcon Heavy, eight months ahead of its commitment date

name: LISA
summary: Three spacecraft 2.5 million km apart, listening for gravitational waves from merging giant black holes.
budgetNote: Figures are NASA's contribution to the ESA mission.

name: HWO
summary: The astrophysics flagship after Roman: built to image Earth-like planets around nearby stars and search them for signs of life.
